claim: json_escape handled \\ " \n \t but not \r, so a value carrying a carriage return still emitted an invalid record — the exact failure the fix exists to prevent
the old duplicate-key behaviour was a spoofing path: agent=someone-else was last-wins, so an agent could attribute its own action to another in the ADR 0003 audit record
a naive refusal mid-loop would append half a record and corrupt the log the refusal protects; validation now completes before any byte is printed

json_escape forks a subshell per key and per value where the old code expanded inline — rejected: guard.sh runs a handful of times per agent run, and one function removes the escape logic duplicated across cmd_log and cmd_finding

cmd_stop swallows cmd_log failure with || true, so a bad pair there would report a successful stop having logged nothing — rejected: stopping the fleet must never fail on a logging error, and the stop file is the thing that matters

PR 43 logSpend passes agent= to guard.sh, which is a reserved key since PR 20 — guard.sh exits 2 and writes nothing, so no usd/tokens ever reach the audit log that fleet cost reads. The repo's own TestRefusesBadPairs/log_reserved_agent proves it, and that test passes in PR 43's own CI.

PR 43 discards logSpend's error with _ =, so the guard.sh refusal above is silent — the run reports a cost in -json while the ledger stays unmeasured, which is the exact split cost.go was written to prevent

PR 43 parseRunReport anchors on the literal {"is_error" so it only parses reports where is_error is the FIRST key; identical data with type first, or pretty-printed, returns unmeasured. Demonstrated by running the parser against reordered copies of its own fixture.
PR 43's fixture was authored alongside the parser, so the test proves the parser matches the fixture rather than the runner — no captured runner output backs the key order it depends on

PR 43 comments Builder.USD as '0 with Measured false means unmeasured' but Builder has no Measured field — Measured is on cost.go's Spend, so a Builder with usd 0 in fleet run -json is genuinely ambiguous

PR 42 retro cites 17 direct-to-main commits; I cannot reproduce 17 under any window — since 2026-08-15 it is 32 including beads: bookkeeping or 10 excluding it. The argument is unaffected but the number needs its definition stated.

the three high findings against PR 43 (reserved agent= key, swallowed error, key-order-dependent parser) are fixed on bead/measure-cost; disposition moves ignored -> accepted, recorded by appending because the ledger is not rewritten
